speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin my assessment, could you please describe exactly where the double vision appears and how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that description; the fact that your vision changes with gaze and your weakness fluctuates with activity is very helpful. To further narrow this down, could you tell me if you experience any difficulty with speaking, swallowing, or drooling during these episodes?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_CHEMISTRY (specifically Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies)
REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes_and_Calcium

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results for acetylcholine receptor antibodies and electrolytes help rule out myasthenia gravis and metabolic causes. Given your worsening weakness after activity and gaze-dependent double vision, could you tell me if you experience any muscle pain or cramping during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: CK (Creatine_Kinase)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal CK level rules out inflammatory myopathies like polymyositis. Given your gaze-dependent diplopia and fatigable weakness without pain or sensory changes, have you noticed any eyelid drooping or difficulty closing your eyes?

REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Decreased muscle response observed with repetitive stimulation
